title: Retained post-replay lineage and compute allocation review
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Recent matched one-million-hand interventions lack replicated own-root breadth; separate changing-regimen lineage from genuine fixed-regimen scale before allocating more compute.
material_change: Zero-hand bounded synthesis of four completed independently audited trials, preserving panel identities, seed dependence and actual cost.
notes: Uses corrected family allocation terminal report. No pooled cross-trial inferential claim or paired cross-stage difference. Throughput355-542 physical/s is confounded by runtime conditions.

result.summary: Bounded four-trial synthesis completed48 retained own-root cells with source hashes and actual wall costs; zero new poker hands.
result.conclusion: No final arm/panel has positive own-root lower confidence bounds in both seeds. One capacity5 control has positive points +0.278/+8.011 but wide CIs and no Seed1 dual-seat gain. Changing regimens are not one stationary long-run curve; evidence insufficient for automatic scale, not universal method failure.
result.decision: Preserve all endpoints. No fresh-only promotion, arbitrary replay/allocation sweep, automatic4M or Slumbot qualification.
result.next_step: Qualify outcome-independent retained temporal policy aggregation versus final iterate as a bounded stability hypothesis, requiring compatible execution contracts and immutable two-seed dose-selected checkpoints before any preregistered evaluation.
